questions.question: Which event triggered the July Crisis in 1914?
choices: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
Germany's invasion of Poland
Russia's invasion of Finland
The fall of the Berlin Wall

choices: Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy
Britain, Germany, and Japan
Britain, France, and Russia
France, Austria-Hungary, and Spain

questions.question: Which two powers were central members of the Central Powers?
choices: Britain and France
Germany and Austria-Hungary
Russia and Italy
United States and Japan

questions.question: What was an armistice?
choices: A treaty guaranteeing permanent neutrality
A plan to divide a colony
An order to begin military conscription
An agreement to stop fighting

questions.question: On what date did the major Western Front armistice take effect?
choices: November 11, 1918
April 6, 1917
September 1, 1939

questions.question: Which treaty imposed the main postwar settlement on Germany?
choices: Treaty of Ghent
Treaty of Tordesillas
Treaty of Versailles
Treaty of Utrecht

questions.question: Which organization was created after the war to promote collective security?
choices: United Nations
League of Nations
Warsaw Pact
European Union

questions.question: How did militarism contribute to tensions?
choices: It required states to dissolve their armed forces
It prevented military influence on policy
It eliminated competition among European powers
Arms buildups and war planning increased readiness for conflict

questions.question: Why did alliances help turn a regional crisis into a wider war?
choices: Governments' commitments and decisions drew additional powers into the conflict
Every alliance legally required immediate war under any circumstance
All European countries belonged to one alliance
Alliances removed leaders' ability to make choices

questions.question: Why did trench warfare produce stalemate on parts of the Western Front?
choices: Neither side had access to artillery
Soldiers fought only from moving ships
Defensive weapons and fortified positions made advances costly
All armies refused to build defensive positions

questions.question: How did imperial competition contribute to prewar tensions?
choices: European empires had no interests outside Europe
Rival powers competed over territory, influence, and resources
Colonial competition ended all nationalist movements
Colonies were excluded from wartime mobilization

questions.question: What made World War I a global conflict?
choices: All fighting occurred within France
Only European civilians experienced disruption
Neutrality prevented every non-European power from participating
Colonial forces and campaigns extended the war beyond Europe

questions.question: Why did Russia leave the war after the Bolsheviks took power?
choices: The new government sought peace and signed Brest-Litovsk
Russia had conquered all of Germany
The United States required Russia to join the Central Powers
The League of Nations ordered a withdrawal in 1914

questions.question: How did total war affect civilian life?
choices: Civilian economies remained separate from military needs
Every factory stopped producing during the conflict
Governments mobilized labor, resources, and public opinion for the war
Only professional soldiers faced government restrictions

questions.question: Why did U.S. entry in 1917 matter to the Allies?
choices: It immediately ended every campaign worldwide
It added substantial financial, material, and eventually military support
It caused Britain to withdraw from the conflict
It restored the Russian monarchy

questions.question: Which order places these World War I events correctly?
choices: U.S. entry, 1918 armistice, Sarajevo assassination
1918 armistice, Sarajevo assassination, U.S. entry
Sarajevo assassination, 1918 armistice, U.S. entry
Sarajevo assassination, U.S. entry, 1918 armistice

questions.question: A government rations food and directs factories toward military supplies. What does this illustrate?
choices: Total-war mobilization
Complete economic neutrality
An end to civilian participation
Restoration of feudal labor

questions.question: Which comparison of the armistice and Versailles treaty is accurate?
choices: Both were signed before the war began
The treaty stopped fighting in 1914; the armistice divided Europe in 1919
The armistice stopped major fighting; the treaty set peace terms afterward
Both were military plans for invading France

questions.question: Why should war causation distinguish long-term tensions from immediate triggers?
choices: The assassination alone explains every military and political decision
The assassination sparked a crisis within an already tense international system
Long-term tensions mean leaders had no choices
The war began without any diplomatic crisis

questions.question: Which postwar change most directly altered Europe's political map?
choices: The formation of NATO in 1918
The unification of every European country
The restoration of all prewar empires unchanged
The collapse of empires and creation or restoration of states
